reader.requirement: At COBOL-85 a character-string that uses more than one of '+', '-', '*', 'Z' and the currency symbol as floating replacement characters (+ with -, a sign with cs, Z with *, either suppression symbol with a floating insertion symbol) must be refused.

edition-consulted.switches: dialectLevel < 2002: a non-floating currency symbol takes only the CurrencyLeading role (the 1985 chart has one fixed cs row/column); also appends the 1985 chart clause to the COBOL1935 message
edition.DialectLevel < 2002 selects the 1985 BLANK WHEN ZERO arm (asterisk only, VI.5.9.3 SR7) over the 2002+ S-or-asterisk arm; message text

reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel/ConstructRegistry/CobolVersion in PictureComposition.cs and PictureAnalyzer.cs. The cells that decide this rule (floating {+-}/cs rows and columns against {Z *}) are the 2023 Table 10 matrix used at every edition; compared by hand with the 1985 chart of VI.5.9.6 (spec md lines 11449-11471): the floating {Z*}-left row is blank in every floating +-/cs column, the floating {+-}-left and cs-left rows are blank in the {Z*} columns, the same as Table10Rows. SR21 (Z/* exclusive) and SR23 (+/- exclusive) are edition-blind.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: every pair is refused by edition-blind code (SR21, SR23, Table-10 cells identical to the 1985 chart); ++$$9 gives the same COBOL1935 at --std 2023.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb530 is legal-source only (+$$$, $$.$$, ++.++); no witness refuses a pair of floating replacement characters

probes.printed: ++$$9, $$++9, $$--9, --$$9: error COBOL1935; ++--9: error COBOL1934 'the editing sign control symbols + and - are mutually exclusive'
cs/+/- with Z or *: COBOL1935; Z with *: COBOL1934

probes.expected: legal: one floating string beside a fixed symbol

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.5.9.5 GR9  (5.9.5 Editing Rules)  the text is in GR9
OK  §1985:VI.5.9.5 GR7  (5.9.5 Editing Rules)  the text is in GR7

reader.notes: Every pair of floating replacement characters probed was refused at --std 85, and a fixed symbol beside one floating string stays legal. The refusal comes from the SR21/SR23 checks and the Table-10 matrix, whose relevant cells match the 1985 chart.

refuter.evidence: --std 85: +---9, -+++9, +(3)-(2)9 (fixed one sign, floating the other, and repeat-factor forms) COBOL1934 '+' and '-' mutually exclusive; ++++CR COBOL1934; $Z$9 COBOL1934 (two cs); ++9+ and $$9$$ (split floating strings) COBOL1935; every cs/+/-/Z/* floating pair refused (see -3 probes). One floating string with a fixed symbol stays legal: -$$$9 [   $1], $$$$+ [  $1+], $$$$CR [  $1  ], $$B$$9 [   $12], B$$9 [ $12]. Later-edition currency forms (CURRENCY "EUR", WITH PICTURE SYMBOL) refused at 85 so no second currency symbol can enter. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VI.5.9.5 GR9  (5.9.5 Editing Rules)  the text is in GR9'.
